MuJoCoCoordinate beyond small straightforward fixes; native tests in double and single precision. Google CLA applies.

vLLM production-stackMajor changes/new architecture use the proposal process; small fixes and simple features are expressly exempt. DCO and applicable CI still required.
Mistral Python SDKGenerated SDK policy refuses direct changes/PRs. A historical merge median does not override the present policy.

Research notes & original sources

The table preserves the 20 September audit. No issue status or policy was refreshed while creating this page.

Methodology & limits

The snapshot is 20 September 2026 in Asia/Kolkata. Final retained-issue state check: 2026-09-19 19:56 UTC (20 September 01:26 IST): all retained issues were OPEN and unassigned, and none had a changed update time/comment count since the detailed audit. PR searches and policy/metrics collection ran earlier in this same research session. Availability is not reserved.

What was checked. Public GitHub history, 77 repository metadata/issue/PR snapshots, 160 detailed issue audits, contributor policies, full fetched issue bodies/comments/timelines, number-reference searches, title searches, and additional semantic searches for likely collisions. Each detailed issue fetch allowed 100 comments and 100 relevant timeline items; pagination flags were inspected. Discovery generally covered the most recently updated 100 open issues per repo (35 for retried large queries), plus selected older leads from your research. Repository discovery is broad but not exhaustive. Semantic searches can miss differently described or newly opened work. Some broad searches were capped; the raw result counts remain in evidence.

What was not checked. No issue reproduction, build, regression suite, paid cloud evaluation or Fable review was executed. GPU=No is an assessment of the proposed validation scope. There is no promise that every lead will reproduce or be accepted. A platform-specific claim must be proved on that platform; mocks do not establish a fix to a closed server or GPU runtime.

Outside merges and median. Fresh cohort: up to 60 MERGED PRs per repo, ordered by updatedAt, not a fixed-time submission cohort or the old 100-PR sample. Remove GitHub bot authors/absent authors; classify OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR as affiliated; inspect public company/current-work biography, current CODEOWNERS/MAINTAINERS, original-project-author evidence, and prior affiliation corrections. Company-style handles and prior uncertain affiliation are conservatively excluded. Remaining authors are *external candidates*, not verified non-employees. Public profile fields can be incomplete, misleading or stale. The accompanying JSON records each PR, classification reason, timestamps and merge duration. Median = median(mergedAt − createdAt) for that external-candidate subset. A dagger means fewer than 10 external-candidate merges. A percentage among merged PRs is not an acceptance probability; unmerged/closed PRs are absent from that calculation. Repository-wide medians are not estimates for a particular issue, difficulty or today's review queue. Recently updated PRs can include very old merges; inspect each repo's date range before relying on it. Old September 18 numbers are preserved but not mixed into the refreshed table.

Career fit. Evaluation/data correctness, simulation state, runtime recovery and SDK/protocol behavior provide more direct ML/AI infrastructure evidence than UI fixes. UI/CLI work can build an initial maintainer relationship but does not establish model-training expertise by itself. Difficulty reflects the proposed scope, test/compatibility burden and design uncertainty, not a LOC quota. Narrowing a scope may change the difficulty category.

Affiliation and exclusions. Qwen, DeepSeek and other China-based company targets are excluded. AIBrix is excluded because its stated origin is ByteDance despite the vLLM namespace: official vLLM announcement. Global community repositories are not excluded based on individual contributors' nationality. Cookbooks and example-only repositories are excluded. DeepSWE is a project/model collaboration associated with Agentica and Together, not a benchmark company: Together's announcement. Together and independent rLLM are tracked separately. MCP is also a separate project bucket, not a second credit toward Anthropic's quota. Harbor's canonical repository is now harbor-framework/harbor.

Your reusable campaign prompt

Build and maintain an evidence-backed OSS contribution campaign for GitHub user rohan-patnaik, supporting a move from an ML engineering role into an AI company, ultimately including OpenAI or Anthropic.

  1. Start from my actual public contribution history and the supplied research, rather than assuming previous issue availability or merge figures are still current. Use the pasted T3 extracts and any accessible records from threads [private research thread], [private research thread] and [private research thread]. Say which records you could access.
  2. Research recognizable and promising AI labs, AI product companies, infrastructure teams, and evaluation/benchmark projects. Group and rank the output by company/team, with OpenAI and Anthropic first. Distinguish company-owned repositories from associated independent projects. Do not count an MCP contribution twice as both MCP and Anthropic, or label rLLM as a Together-owned repository. Verify affiliations.
  3. Exclude China-based company repositories and cookbook/example-only repositories. Do not exclude a global project merely because an individual contributor is Chinese or a test mentions a Chinese model. Exclude work whose convincing reproduction or validation requires a GPU or other unavailable accelerator. Linux, Windows and macOS are available; the Linux laptop has a Ryzen 7 5800H and about 16 GiB RAM. Flag required VMs, Docker, cloud accounts, paid API calls, large downloads and platform-specific testing. A CPU mock does not establish that an accelerator-specific bug is fixed.
  4. Keep a 2–2–2 ledger for each company/team: two genuinely low, two medium and two high contributions, possibly across different repositories. The eventual goal is at least 100 useful PRs; 17 complete six-PR portfolios produce 102. If all screened teams remain in scope, calculate that larger total. Do not split one fix artificially, inflate difficulty, double-count the same contribution or fill missing slots with claimed, fixed, unwanted or unverifiable issues. Report gaps explicitly.
  5. Prioritize existing open issues. Check issue bodies, all available comments, labels, assignments, linked/timeline PRs, same-number references, and semantic/title/code-path PR searches. An unassigned issue with no linked PR can still be claimed. Read prior closed PRs and maintainer decisions. Distinguish “no matching PR found at this timestamp” from proof that none exists. Verify current source ownership and reproducibility before calling a candidate ready.
  6. For each lead, show company/team, repository and issue link, low/medium/high category, career signal, external contribution policy and observed outside participation, median creation-to-merge time for the stated merged-PR cohort, why it fits and remaining gate, GPU requirement, and whether an existing or overlapping PR was found. Include the snapshot time, methodology and sample size. Never treat outsiders' share among merged PRs as an acceptance probability. Open PRs have no realized merge time; report backlog separately where useful.
  7. Audit contribution agreements and AI-assistance rules per repository. I already report having signed Google, Microsoft and Meta CLAs. Check public status evidence where possible. List any additional agreements with official reading/signing links; distinguish an unknown signature from a confirmed missing public record. Distinguish a CLA, a DCO commit sign-off, and an issue-approval/assignment gate. Do not sign agreements on my behalf.
  8. This stage is research and planning. Do not publish issues, claim work, open PRs, start the remote review workflow or open browser windows yet. Do not claim local reproductions or tests that were not run.
  9. In a later discovery stage, search recent Reddit, Hacker News, X/Twitter and relevant community discussions for recurring complaints. Trace each complaint to an editable upstream repository, check its version and ownership, deduplicate it, reproduce it with a minimal test where possible, then follow that project's issue/security process. A forum complaint is a lead, not proof of a bug. Credit original reporters and coordinate with existing contributors; being first cannot be guaranteed.
  10. Once I select work and authorize implementation, use GPT-6 Astra in the authoring T3 thread to reproduce the issue, implement a focused fix and regression tests, and prepare a draft PR. Respect any repository rule requiring approval before even a draft PR. Capture the exact commit, commands, results and platform evidence.
  11. Obtain independent review from the requested Fable 5.1 model in a new T3 Code thread on my Mac the designated review Mac. First verify that host and exact model are available; do not silently substitute another model or claim a review that did not run. Transfer only the relevant review material and identify the exact commit reviewed.
  12. Evaluate every review finding independently. Record accept/reject/defer with reasons; reproduce substantive claims, revise valid findings while the PR stays draft, and rerun affected checks. A model's approval does not replace test evidence. If the commit changes materially, refresh the review against the updated commit.
  13. When implementation, review reconciliation and verification are complete, leave the PR in draft and open exactly one chosen draft PR in Chrome for me to review. This browser step belongs to that later stage. Provide the PR link, final commit, tests, reviewer findings and remaining limitations. Do not merge or mark ready without my instruction.

Optimize for useful, defensible contributions and sustained maintainer relationships. Treat the 100-PR objective as a campaign target, not a claim that 100 suitable issues are currently available.
